metadata.title: AI@UNCW Project Dashboard
metadata.identity: The AI Hub Orchestrates and GAABS Supports AI Builders.
metadata.subidentity: GAABS is the advanced tool-building arm within The AI Hub.
metadata.publicNotice: This public dashboard contains approved summary information only. Project-file-only information is not live-verified.

executiveSummary: The AI Hub website is live. Summer AI Institute programming was delivered successfully as a CTE and CSE initiative, and the August 5 University Advancement hands-on AI build workshop was reported very successful. AI Currents has been established as a Viva Engage discussion community for the UNCW ecosystem and was reported off to a strong start. These statements establish activity and reported status, not participation levels, outcomes, effectiveness, or continuing support commitments. Governance, fall programming, research-capacity work, and the DS&AI consulting-center pilot remain bounded by their stated approval and readiness conditions.
priorities: Await final senior approval of the AI Hub Advisory Board memo sent to the Provost; membership and invitations remain unapproved
Plan an open-to-all fall AI discussion and lecture series that complements CTE's faculty-focused programming; speakers, dates, and partnerships remain unconfirmed
Keep the AI for Research Lunch and Learn and researcher map as draft work and catalytic research support and a faculty research AI champion as exploratory concepts
Confirm student appointments, access and budget, authorized scope, validation, maintenance, and a separately authorized initial project before experimental DS&AI consulting-center pilot work begins
Preserve public review, approval, delivery, commitment, and evidence boundaries

risks.statement: Transmission or review of the AI Hub Advisory Board memo could be mistaken for final approval, approved membership, or invitation authority.
risks.mitigation: State that the memo was sent to the Provost and awaits final senior approval; keep membership and invitations unapproved and unauthorized.

risks.statement: AI advisory work could be misunderstood as replacing established shared governance.
risks.mitigation: State advisory limits explicitly and recognize existing authorities.

risks.statement: A future workshop could face access, network, pacing, or login issues if participant-path testing and a fallback are not completed.
risks.mitigation: Apply the Summer AI Institute lesson: test the complete participant path and maintain a safe no-login fallback before delivery.

risks.statement: New commitments could exceed available capacity if they are added without identifying what they displace.
risks.mitigation: Avoid adding commitments without identifying what they displace and protect scheduled delivery work.

risks.statement: The shared consultation model could be described inaccurately as GAABS-owned or GAABS-only.
risks.mitigation: Use shared-space language that recognizes Library facilitation and the broader consultation role.

risks.statement: The completed EDU-license rollout could be misrepresented as an effectiveness study even though it was not systematic or study-coordinated.
risks.mitigation: Describe available evidence only as descriptive adoption monitoring and require advance coordination before any future prospective evaluation.

risks.statement: The stale July 21 scheduled cross-system item could be interpreted as confirmed attendance, partnership, endorsement, transfer, commitment, or follow-up.
risks.mitigation: Mark the outcome as needing verification and make no new external relationship or endorsement claim without a separate confirmed update.

risks.statement: Post-launch website content could be mistaken for approved policy or broad service availability.
risks.mitigation: Preserve review and ownership boundaries for future content and correct material issues promptly.

risks.statement: A possible educational agent could duplicate static guidance or imply endorsement before its purpose and maintenance model are clear.
risks.mitigation: Establish the article baseline, audience, source ownership, and agent-specific value before committing to build it.

risks.statement: The experimental DS&AI consulting-center pilot could begin without student appointments, access and budget, authorized scope, validation, maintenance, or a separately authorized initial project.
risks.mitigation: Confirm every condition before pilot work begins; do not describe the model as a production service.

risks.statement: Student turnover could leave an early prototype without a maintainer.
risks.mitigation: Use peer learning, document handoff responsibilities, and name continuity ownership before implementation.

risks.statement: The first pilot could become too technically ambitious for its client need or cohort readiness.
risks.mitigation: Favor maintainable solutions and confirm authorized scope, validation criteria, maintenance ownership, and the initial project before implementation.

risks.statement: Delivered programming or reported success could be interpreted as attendance, participant-outcome evidence, tool performance, effectiveness, or a continuing support commitment.
risks.mitigation: Report delivery separately from attendance, participant outcomes, tool performance, effectiveness, and future support commitments.

risks.statement: Draft or exploratory research activity could be interpreted as an established program, funded support, or an approved role.
risks.mitigation: Keep the Lunch and Learn and researcher map as draft work and catalytic support and the faculty-champion idea exploratory until their approval conditions are met.

risks.statement: AI Currents' reported strong start could be converted into unsupported membership, engagement, outcome, moderation, or support claims.
risks.mitigation: Keep the statement qualitative and explicitly reported; add quantitative, outcome, moderation, or support claims only with separate evidence and authorization.

risks.statement: Fall series planning could be interpreted as confirmed programming, speakers, dates, or partnerships.
risks.mitigation: Describe the series as active planning that complements CTE's faculty-focused programming and keep speakers, dates, and partnerships unconfirmed.
